title: Effects of continued administration of empagliflozin in patients with heart failure on active SGLT2 inhibitor treatment admitted for acute decompensated heart failure
official: Effects of continued administration of empagliflozin in patients with heart failure on active SGLT2 inhibitor treatment admitted for acute decompensated heart failure
summary: Main objective: To assess the non-inferiority of continued administration of empagliflozin 10 mg versus placebo plus standard medical care in patients admitted with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) with prior treatment using a SGLT2 inhibitor on the combined endpoint of all-cause mortality, HF hospitalization and worsening renal function at 90 days after admission.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients (age ≥ 18 years) with acute decompensated heart failure (HF) according to clinical assessment on active therapy with a SGLT2 inhibitor
2. Brain Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) >100 pg/ml or N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) >300 pg/ml
3. Written informed consent obtained
4. Negative pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential
Exclusion criteria:
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus
2. Identification of any causes of heart failure leading to decompensation that needs urgent management (like acute coronary syndrome, severe unstable arrhythmias, mechanical causes, acute pulmonary embolism)
3. Incapacity to understand and / or to provide written informed consent
4. Obvious uncontrolled substance abuse
5. Pregnancy, breastfeeding
6. Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) with eGFR<20 ml/min, or end-stage renal failure with the need for chronic dialysis treatment
7. Acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring dialysis treatment
8. Known intolerance to empagliflozin
9. Acute heart failure without signs of congestion (“dry” patient)
10. Indication for coronary angiography or any foreseeable administration of a contrast media
11. Need for hemofiltration or any other form of extracorporeal therapy
12. Planned surgery
13. Previous participation in this trial or recent participation in another clinical trial (within the last 4 weeks before inclusion)
